claims.text: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 79 seconds, from 06:28:20 to 06:29:39, before cancelling at 06:29:42. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The shortfall is 101 seconds, so the cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full under POL-NS-06.

The dwell cannot be extended by summing separate in-geofence intervals: the trace shows a single in-geofence run (run_count 1), so there is no second interval for POL-NS-06(i) to add, and in any event the traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02730-01 is MISSING, which makes limb (i) unavailable on its own terms. The 79-second dwell is the whole of the driver's qualifying presence.

The rider was at the pickup point and actively coordinating. Her device track places her within 15.7 to 23.2 metres of the pin for all 30 of her fixes, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and she sent the message 'coming out now' at 06:29:20, 22 seconds before the driver cancelled at 06:29:42. The driver never replied and no in-app call is recorded. Under POL-NS-04 the rider is exonerated and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 06:28:20 is corroborated by the trace: the first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the same timestamp with a dwell_start_offset_sec of 0.0, so the arrival marker is not false and POL-NS-05 does not apply. The case therefore turns purely on the dwell arithmetic of POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-06, and the driver's own arrival is what defeats his fee.

The fare ledger confirms the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. That is the amount the rider contests and the amount that must be returned to her; the refund is of the cancellation-fee line only.

The driver's counter-statement asks the tribunal to decide on the rider's history of no-shows. That is reputation reasoning, not evidence about this trip. rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the field POL-NS-09(d) reads; the citable trailing-window field, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, is 1, far below the threshold of 3 that limb (d) requires. The profile cannot carry an adverse finding here.

The driver's own profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against completed_trips_30d of 65, a rate of roughly 0.015, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and no escalation is triggered on that ground. The driver's payout question is therefore decided on the ordinary rule, and because the fee is not chargeable at all there is no compensation to pay.

The rider's claim that she cancelled after under two minutes is not quite the record: the trip was terminated by the DRIVER at 06:29:42, about 9.5 minutes after acceptance, under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. I do not rely on the rider's own characterisation of the cancellation; the refund follows from the driver's short dwell and the rider's unanswered coordination message, not from the timing the rider asserted.

claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 79 seconds, from 06:28:20 to 06:29:39, with 9 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-02's arrival test is met and POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 06:28:20 and a wait timer started at 06:28:22, and the driver terminated the trip at 06:29:42 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event — POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are therefore satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The rider's own track shows 30 fixes, all at 0.0 kph, between 15.7 m and 23.2 m of the pickup pin across the waiting window — the rider's device was stationary at the pin, which is consistent with a rider who was present but did not board, and it is not evidence of a driver who failed to arrive.

The rider's single chat message 'coming out now' was sent at 06:29:20 and read at 06:29:40, and the driver cancelled at 06:29:42 — the rider was still on the way out of the building when the trip was terminated, which is the factual core of a no-show rather than a driver-side coordination failure.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged and payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and that figure reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50 for this trip, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare-integrity defect to disturb the charge.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, which is below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 65 is 0.015, below the 0.08 rate — so compensation is payable rather than withheld.
Compensation is therefore fixed by POL-NS-07 at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force, which the fare ledger computes as SGD 3.60, the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee.

I concede that the effective in-geofence dwell of 79 seconds falls short of the 180 second free waiting period in force for this STANDARD zone by 101 seconds, so POL-NS-06 on its face would refund the fee; the driver's answer is POL-NS-06 limb (i), which requires a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02730-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so limb (i) is unavailable and I do not press it.

I further concede that the driver's arrival marker was a BUTTON press rather than GPS_AUTO, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed-arrival shortcut is not available and the arrival and dwell must be read from the exported trace alone.

The driver's counterparty statement asks the tribunal to look at the rider's history of no-shows; I do not rely on rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags, which is a lifetime counter and is context only under POL-GEN-01, and the only citable rider counter, no_show_disputes_30d at 1, is below the POL-NS-09(d) threshold of 3 and so does not escalate this case.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is supported, and the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full. To the driver: the fee is not chargeable, but this is not a finding that you were dishonest — it is the waiting-period arithmetic, and it is decided on your own telemetry.

The platform's records agree on the timeline. You were assigned and accepted the trip at 06:20:13, tapped 'I'm Here' at 06:28:20, and terminated the trip at 06:29:42 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four of its conditions hold. Limb (a) is satisfied (the arrived event is present), and limb (b) is satisfied (the exported GPS trace puts you inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival geofence at 06:28:20, the same instant, with a dwell_start_offset of 0.0). Limb (c) fails. Your qualifying in-geofence presence is a single continuous run of 79 seconds, from 06:28:20 to 06:29:39, carrying 9 qualifying fixes. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). 79 seconds is 101 seconds short. Limb (d) therefore also fails, because the record does not show the trip terminated at or after the required dwell elapsed — the required dwell never elapsed. Where any of the four limbs fails the fee is not chargeable, and the applicable refund clause here is POL-NS-06.

The 79-second figure cannot be increased. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present, populated traffic_advisory with a qualifying type covers the pickup road, and only where there is more than one interval to sum. There is a single in-geofence run (run_count 1), and the advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02730-01 is MISSING, so limb (i) is unavailable on its own terms as well as inapplicable. I note that the driver-side and rider-side claims resting on that artifact were discarded by the referee for non-disclosure of its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue, which is correct.

On the driver's remaining points: your claim that limbs (a) and (d) hold is accepted only as to (a); (d) fails for the reason above, and (c) fails outright, so the conjunctive test of POL-NS-01 is not met. Your claim that compensation is fixed at SGD 3.60 under POL-NS-07 is rejected: POL-NS-07 pays compensation only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-06 displaces it here. There is therefore no driver compensation, and the anti-farming check on driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against completed_trips_30d of 65 (rate 0.015) is never reached. Your claim that the fare ledger reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd and shows no POL-NS-08(d) defect is accepted — the charged line of SGD 4.50 equals the net figure — and it is why no fare-integrity issue disturbs the refund.

On the rider's points: the POL-NS-04 exoneration argument (unanswered 'coming out now' message, rider stationary 15.7–23.2 m from the pin throughout) is not needed, because POL-NS-06 already refunds the fee in full with no driver compensation; it would reach the same result. The driver's arrival marker was a true one — the trace fixes you at the pin at the moment of the tap — so POL-NS-05 does not apply and no false-arrival referral arises. POL-NS-12 does not apply because the marker is a BUTTON press, not GPS_AUTO, which both sides correctly concede.

No escalation arises. There is no POL-NS-08(a)–(d) impairment: clock skew is nil at arrival, the trace has no gaps over 120 seconds (max gap 0.0) and carries the rider track, the chat log's single message matches chat_message_count 1 with intact numbering, and the fare line reconciles to the net fee. There is no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts, no POL-NS-09(c) counterparty-dispute pattern, and no POL-NS-09(d) trigger — the citable rider counter rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3. The driver's counterparty statement asking the tribunal to consider the rider's no-show history is treated as it must be: reputation is not a ground of decision, and rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 makes context only. I have not used it as a ground against the rider in either direction.

Confidence is 0.90. The deciding fact — the 79-second qualifying dwell against the 180-second free wait — is carried by the GPS trace EV-GPS-02730 and the trip record EV-TRIP-02730, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02 cap is 1.0. No referral is produced: no clause in this category directs one on these facts, and the false-arrival referral provision of POL-NS-05 is not engaged. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the POL-GEN-05 automatic-execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes on issue subject to appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
The disputed amount is the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee on trip TRP-02730 (EV-FARE-02730, total_charged 4.50; the same figure is platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd in EV-TRIP-02730). That fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full. No driver compensation is payable.

Why the fee fails. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. The driver did arrive: EV-GPS-02730 shows one continuous run of 9 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:28:20 to 06:29:39 (79 seconds), and EV-TRIP-02730 carries the 'arrived' event at 06:28:20, so limbs (a) and (b) are met. Limb (c) is not. The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds (EV-TRIP-02730, platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the arrival tap. The driver held position 79 seconds and cancelled at 06:29:42 — a 101-second shortfall. Limb (d) fails for the same reason: the termination did not fall at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. POL-NS-06 therefore applies on its own terms (effective dwell shorter than the free waiting period) and refunds the cancellation fee in full, with no compensation.

Independently, POL-NS-04. The rider sent 'coming out now' at 06:29:20 (EV-CHAT-02730); the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call (EV-TRIP-02730, in_app_calls empty) before cancelling 22 seconds later; and the rider's track places her device 15.7–23.2 m from the pin on all 30 fixes, well inside the 100 m STANDARD radius. On those limbs the rider is exonerated with no driver compensation. Either route reaches the same result.

What I did with the arguments. The driver's arrival and fare-integrity points are accepted: the arrival is genuine (EV-GPS-02730, dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so POL-NS-05 does not fire and no false-arrival referral arises, and the 4.50 charge reconciles with platform_policy, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect. The driver's concession that the marker is a BUTTON press (POL-NS-12) is accepted — the platform-confirmed-arrival shortcut is unavailable, and the arrival and dwell are read from the exported trace, which is what shows the 79-second dwell. The GPS trace, trip record, chat log and fare ledger all carry weight 1.0 and none is impaired, so the confidence cap on the deciding fact (the 79-second dwell against the 180-second minimum) is 1.0. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold and executes on issue unless either party appeals under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02730 is refunded in full to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the charge does not stand. To charge a no-show fee the driver had to hold position inside the pickup geofence for the free waiting period in force (POL-NS-01 limb (c)). The record's platform_policy puts that period at 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and the fare ledger carries the same 180 s). On the driver's own telemetry (EV-GPS-02730) he held position in-geofence for a single continuous run of 79 seconds, from 06:28:20 to 06:29:39, and terminated the trip at 06:29:42 under RIDER_NO_SHOW — a shortfall of 101 seconds. POL-NS-06 therefore makes the fee not chargeable and refunds it in full, and POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails, so the fee cannot stand under the anchor clause either. The rider's suggestion that she 'cancelled after under two minutes' is not the record — the driver cancelled, about 9.5 minutes after acceptance — but the refund does not rest on her timing; it rests on the driver's short dwell.

POL-NS-06 limb (i). Both sides' accumulation arguments were discarded at Step 1: limb (i) needs a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02730-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0. Neither advocate disclosed that impairment and its issue code (MISSING_ARTIFACT) in the claim, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires, so the claims were discarded. I reach the same substantive conclusion anyway: there is a single in-geofence run, so there is no second interval to sum.

The arrival marker (POL-NS-05). At 06:28:20 the trace places the driver in-geofence at a dwell_start_offset of 0.0 s. He was not more than 300 m from the pin and not travelling at or above 15 km/h, so the 'I'm Here' marker is not false, POL-NS-05 does not fire, and no false-arrival referral arises under POL-NS-05(ii).

Driver compensation (POL-NS-07). The driver is paid only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies. POL-NS-01 fails at limb (c), and this was a driver-initiated termination, not a rider cancellation after the dwell had elapsed, so limb (g) does not apply either. The anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1, rate 0.015, both under the POL-NS-07 thresholds), but that is beside the point: with no chargeable fee there is nothing to pay 80 percent of. The claim for SGD 3.60 compensation (80 percent of SGD 4.50) is rejected.

Rider presence and contact (POL-NS-04). The rider's device sat 15.7–23.2 m from the pin across all 30 of her fixes, inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and she messaged 'coming out now' at 06:29:20 — 22 seconds before the driver cancelled and cancelled without replying. Those facts independently support a full refund and are consistent with it; the outcome does not need them.

Counter-statement and profiles (POL-GEN-01). The driver's statement invites the tribunal to weigh the rider's no-show history. prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and is context only — it cannot carry an adverse finding about this trip. The citable trailing figure, no_show_disputes_30d, is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires, so no escalation arises on that ground.

No escalation is triggered under POL-NS-09: confidence is above the 0.70 floor; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the same-party repeat-dispute counts are both 0; the anti-farming check is clear; and the deciding artifact (EV-GPS-02730, weight 1.0) is COMPLETE, not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d). The fare ledger reconciles with the net fee under POL-NS-08(d) (4.50 = 4.50), so there is no fare-integrity defect. No clause produces a referral on these facts.

Confidence and execution. The deciding fact — the short in-geofence dwell — is carried by EV-GPS-02730 (weight 1.0) and corroborated by the trip record's own events; the cap is 1.0 and nothing is discounted, so confidence is stated at 0.90. The amount refunded is SGD 4.50, the cancellation-fee line charged on EV-FARE-02730 (total_charged 4.50, fee_charged 4.50, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Driver compensation is null. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is at or below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 this ruling executes automatically.
